recipes.name: Cornmeal porridge
steps: Whisk cornmeal into 250 ml cool water until smooth.
Simmer remaining water with cinnamon in a saucepan.
Whisk in cornmeal slurry and stir constantly for 5 minutes.
Cook over low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring and adding liquid if thick.
Stir in milk, nutmeg and sugar; simmer 3 minutes and serve hot.
recipes.note: Take care: thick porridge splashes when boiling.
recipes.context: Plantation, market and everyday household food traditions

recipes.name: Saltfish fritters
steps: Soak and simmer salted cod in fresh water, repeat if necessary and remove bones.
Mix flour and baking powder; stir in water for a thick batter.
Fold in flaked cod, chopped scallion, onion, thyme and sweet pepper.
Heat a shallow layer of oil over medium heat; drop in small spoonfuls without crowding.
Fry until browned on both sides and fully cooked inside; drain.
recipes.note: Taste cod before seasoning batter; saltiness varies.

recipes.name: Bammy
ingredients: 500 g commercially prepared, food-safe grated cassava
steps: Use only properly processed, food-safe cassava; press out excess moisture.
Mix cassava evenly with salt and divide into eight portions.
Shape flat rounds and cook slowly on a lightly oiled skillet until they hold together and lightly color.
Pour coconut milk into a shallow dish; briefly soak the partially cooked rounds.
Return to the pan and cook gently until hot and cooked through.
recipes.note: Never use raw bitter cassava without professionally validated detoxification; prepared frozen bammy is the safest shortcut.
recipes.context: Indigenous cassava continuities and changed techniques

recipes.name: Roast breadfruit
steps: Wash breadfruit and cut a shallow cross in its base; pierce skin to vent steam.
Roast on an outdoor grill over moderate indirect heat, turning, until all sides char and the flesh is tender, often 45–70 minutes.
Allow to cool enough to handle and remove charred skin and central core.
Cut into wedges and serve with saltfish, fish or vegetables.
For leftovers, pan-fry cooled wedges in a little oil.
recipes.note: Do not leave roasting breadfruit unattended; ensure center is completely cooked.

recipes.name: Coconut rice
steps: Combine coconut milk, water, scallions, thyme and salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add rinsed rice and stir once.
Cover tightly; reduce heat to low and cook about 18–22 minutes without repeated stirring.
Turn off heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Remove aromatics, fluff and serve.
recipes.note: Liquid requirements vary with rice variety.

recipes.name: Jerk chicken
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet, seeded for less heat
steps: Blend allspice, scallion, garlic, bonnet, lime, thyme, soy and oil into a paste.
Coat chicken and refrigerate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight; discard used marinade.
Heat a covered grill for indirect cooking; add a small amount of suitable smoking wood if available.
Cook away from direct flames, turning occasionally, until all pieces reach 74°C/165°F internally.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with festival or rice and peas.
recipes.note: Scotch bonnet is very hot; wear gloves. A modern grill version is not a reconstruction of historical jerk.

recipes.name: Curried chicken
steps: Season chicken with half the curry powder, garlic and thyme; refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot and gently bloom remaining curry powder for 20–30 seconds without burning.
Add chicken and onion; brown lightly for 5 minutes.
Add water, cover and simmer 20 minutes, then add potatoes.
Cook until potatoes soften and chicken reaches 74°C/165°F; adjust liquid and seasoning.
recipes.note: Jamaican curry blends and household practices differ; recipe is an editorial adaptation.

recipes.name: Ital vegetable stew
ingredients: 200 g callaloo or washed leafy greens
steps: Wash and chop vegetables into bite-size pieces; prepare green banana safely using a knife rather than bare hands if sap irritates skin.
Simmer pumpkin, carrot, banana and onion in coconut milk and 200 ml water.
After 10 minutes add chickpeas, thyme and scallion.
Add greens and cook another 8–12 minutes, until all vegetables are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning according to household practice; serve hot.
recipes.note: Not all Rastafari practitioners use the same ingredients or salt guidelines.

recipes.name: Steamed snapper
steps: Check fish for scales and bones; refrigerate until needed.
Warm oil in a wide lidded pan; cook onion, carrot and bell pepper for 4 minutes.
Add tomato, scallion, thyme and water, then simmer 5 minutes.
Nestle fish into the seasoned liquid, cover and cook gently 8–14 minutes depending on thickness.
Check center reaches 63°C/145°F or flesh is opaque and flakes; serve with cooking liquor.
recipes.note: Whole fish and portions contain bones; choose responsibly sourced fish.

recipes.name: Pepper shrimp
steps: Wash hands and equipment after handling raw shrimp and hot pepper.
Mix shrimp with minced garlic, pepper, allspice, paprika and salt.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook shrimp in one layer, turning after 2 minutes.
Add water, cover for 1–2 minutes and continue cooking until shrimp are opaque and firm.
Serve promptly; adjust pepper cautiously.
recipes.note: This is a home skillet interpretation, not a documented Middle Quarters vendor formula.

recipes.name: Banana fritters
steps: Mash bananas until smooth.
Mix with beaten egg, vanilla and sugar.
Stir flour, baking powder and cinnamon into the banana mixture to form a spoonable batter.
Heat shallow oil over medium heat and drop tablespoon portions, leaving space.
Fry until golden and cooked through on both sides; drain and serve.
recipes.note: Very ripe bananas add sweetness; vary sugar to taste.

recipes.name: Ginger beer
steps: Wash and roughly chop ginger; blend with 400 ml water.
Pour over remaining water, stir and refrigerate covered for 2 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth.
Stir in sugar until dissolved and add lime juice.
Chill and serve; refrigerate leftovers and use promptly.
recipes.note: This is a nonfermented fresh ginger drink, not a fermented beer.
